nodes.name: Sandbox User
nodes.description: Human or orchestrating agent who logs in at the IdP and asks mediatore for a sandbox. Never talks to Kubernetes, SPIRE or the hypervisor directly; the broker is the only front door for delegated sandboxes.

nodes.name: Identity Provider (Dex, Google, Auth0, Entra ID)
nodes.description: Upstream OIDC issuer, any the configuration names (ADR-0017): Dex bridging GitHub or LDAP, Google, Auth0, all on the session path (a public PKCE client, the refresh grant before every issue, ADR-0013); Entra ID also performs the On-Behalf-Of exchange (ADR-0016): the caller's access token for mediatore is exchanged at claim creation for a refresh token issued to mediatore for that user, and every token issue is a refresh_token grant naming the audience's resource. mediatore's own STS stands in for delegation on issuers without one (ADR-0003).

nodes.name: mediatore
nodes.description: The identity broker: one binary, two listeners (user-facing bearer HTTPS behind the ingress, sandbox-facing SPIFFE mTLS terminated in-process on aws-lc-rs), a claim watcher and a token backend per audience (ADR-0002, ADR-0003, ADR-0007). Runs as a restricted, non-root Deployment in banlieue-system; its SVID lives only in process memory.

nodes.name: User API (bearer)
nodes.description: POST/GET/DELETE /v1/claims. Validates the caller's IdP token (issuer, audience, signature via JWKS, group gate) and creates an AgentSandbox in the configured namespace with spec.subject taken from the validated token (ADR-0008); GET answers from the resource's status, DELETE deletes it and the finalizer does the rest. Under dev_mode the in-memory store and dev binder stand in. crates/mediatore-api + mediatore-entra.

nodes.name: Sandbox API (SPIFFE mTLS)
nodes.description: POST /v1/nodes, GET /v1/me, POST /v1/token over SPIFFE mTLS: client certificate required, chain verified against the trust-domain bundle, peer SPIFFE ID taken from the verified URI SAN and restricted to /banlieue/node/* and /banlieue/claim/*. Node identities may register and fetch their subject, claim identities may request audience-scoped tokens. The dev header exists only under dev_mode on a loopback listener (ADR-0007). crates/mediatore-api.

nodes.name: Claim Watcher and AgentSandbox Reconciler
nodes.description: Reconciles AgentSandbox (ADR-0008, built): creates and owns one VirtualMachineClaim per sandbox, named after it, at most once; writes the store record keyed by the claim's UID; mirrors the claim's status plus whether the entry is set (Ready only when Bound and set); refuses, before any claim exists, a sandbox naming an audience or issuer outside mediatore's configuration; holds a finalizer that releases the record, deletes the claim and lets the object go only once the claim is gone. Watches VirtualMachineClaim (managed-by label) and VirtualMachine (pool members): on Bound resolves the node by the EK hash the claim mirrors (never by name, address or UUID), binds through the Reconciler, fails an unresolved bind after a bounded wait by deleting the claim, releases on Releasing / Failed / deletion and at resync; declares a node entry when a member publishes its vTPM endorsement certificate; one replica leads by Lease (ADR-0011, built). Never holds a SPIRE admin identity (ADR-0006). crates/mediatore-claims.

nodes.name: STS
nodes.description: Self-issued ES256 tokens with an RFC 8693 act claim naming the claim SVID as actor; JWKS derived from the signing key and served at /.well-known/jwks.json. Used for audiences whose backend is `sts` (ADR-0003). crates/mediatore-sts.

nodes.name: AgentSandbox resources
nodes.description: Namespaced CRD mediatore.io/v1alpha1, served and reconciled by mediatore (ADR-0008, built: roadmap 08; schema generated from the Rust type into deploy/base/crds). The request for one sandbox: subject, poolRef, ttlSeconds, audiences, workload. Created by the user API on POST /v1/claims or declaratively by anything with RBAC on agentsandboxes; spec.subject is pinned to the caller by the mediatore-agentsandbox-subject admission policy unless the caller is mediatore's ServiceAccount or a listed broker, and the whole spec is immutable afterwards. Never carries a credential. Owns exactly one VirtualMachineClaim; a finalizer holds it until the claim and its ClusterStaticEntry are gone. Status mirrors the claim plus whether the entry is set.

nodes.name: Claim Store
nodes.description: Per-claim rows keyed by the claim's UID: a copy of the AgentSandbox request fields (subject, audiences, workload, TTL), the SPIRE entry id, the node id, the sealed refresh envelope (key id, nonce, AES-256-GCM ciphertext bound to the claim UID; ADR-0012 decision 3), the bind deadline and the revocation timestamp; node rows keyed by EK hash; audit rows written when a claim row is swept; sessions rows (a delegated refresh token, sealed, keyed by the AgentSandbox UID) between the API call and the record (ADR-0013). One sqlx implementation over SQLite or PostgreSQL (ADR-0012, built: roadmap 05), the engine chosen by store.url; in-memory only under dev_mode. The resource is the source of truth for the request fields; the store is where revocation and the node registry survive a restart. crates/mediatore-store.

nodes.name: Store Database (PostgreSQL / SQLite)
nodes.description: The engine behind the claim store, chosen by configuration (ADR-0012): PostgreSQL at work, reached only over TLS with sslmode=verify-full on rustls (aws-lc-rs, post-quantum-first key exchange) with the URL in a Secret; SQLite in WAL mode on a volume for a single-replica homelab. Migrations are embedded in the broker and applied at startup under sqlx's lock. Refresh material reaches it sealed; the wrapping key is a Secret volume (local sealer) or stays in OpenBao (transit sealer, ADR-0015).

nodes.name: OpenBao (transit)
nodes.description: Encryption as a service for the refresh envelopes (ADR-0015): the transit engine holds the derived sealing key, encrypts and decrypts on request with the binding UID as context, authorises every call by a token it issued to the broker's ServiceAccount (Kubernetes auth, audience openbao) and rotates the key in place. Since ADR-0016 the same engine may hold the RSA key that signs the broker's client assertion for Entra (transit sign, PSS), so the credential that lets mediatore act as itself at Entra never enters the process. Reached over TLS the broker verifies against a configured CA. In kind: make kind-openbao.

nodes.name: STS Signing Key
nodes.description: EC P-256 private key the STS signs with. File-based in the homelab, OpenBao transit at work. Whoever holds it can mint tokens for any configured audience: guarded asset (threat model TB-1).

nodes.name: Sealing Key
nodes.description: The key that wraps refresh material before it reaches the store (ADR-0012 decision 3). Work shape (ADR-0015): a derived transit key inside OpenBao that never leaves it; the broker holds only a short-lived OpenBao token obtained with its projected ServiceAccount token, and the binding UID is the derivation context. Homelab shape: a 32-byte key from a Secret volume, read into broker memory at start (local sealer).

nodes.name: Kubernetes API Server
nodes.description: Management-cluster API server. mediatore creates and watches AgentSandbox and VirtualMachineClaim through it, and declares SPIRE registration entries as ClusterStaticEntry resources through it. The mediatore-agentsandbox-subject VAP pins spec.subject to the caller except for mediatore's ServiceAccount and listed brokers (ADR-0008); banlieue's claim-subject VAP does the same for claims, with mediatore's ServiceAccount as a listed broker; the mediatore-clusterstaticentry VAP restricts the broker's ServiceAccount to the two entry shapes under /banlieue/ (ADR-0006).

nodes.name: banlieue Control Plane
nodes.description: Schedules pool members and binds VirtualMachineClaims to Ready VMs. mediatore consumes its CRDs (banlieue-api types) and never bypasses it; the Kubernetes API is the only interface between the two (banlieue non-negotiable #1, mediatore ADR-0002).

nodes.name: SPIRE Server (downstream)
nodes.description: The environment-scoped SPIRE server: holds the TPM attestor, the EK trust bundle and the k8s_psat config for this cluster, and issues node identities and workload SVIDs. Its registration entries are rendered by the SPIRE Controller Manager in the same pod over a private Unix socket; no admin API is reachable over the network. mediatore's two entry kinds (/banlieue/node/<ek-hash>, /banlieue/claim/<uid>, ADR-0004) arrive as ClusterStaticEntry resources (ADR-0006). In the enterprise topology it chains to the root via an intermediate CA; in the homelab it is the whole tree (ADR-0005). The TPM node attestor is spiffe/spire-tpm-plugin as a kustomize component (deploy/spire-tpm: an init container from the digest-pinned image, the checksum in server.conf) and its EK trust bundle is one swtpm local CA issuing certificate per hypervisor host, copied beside the plugin by the init container (ADR-0018).

nodes.name: SPIRE Controller Manager
nodes.description: Runs beside the SPIRE server in the same pod (leader-elected across replicas). Watches ClusterSPIFFEID and ClusterStaticEntry resources and renders them into server registration entries over a private Unix socket. The only writer of entries in the cluster; reports status.rendered / masked / set on each resource (ADR-0006).

nodes.name: ClusterStaticEntry resources
nodes.description: Cluster-scoped declarations of mediatore's registration entries: mediatore-node-<ek-hash> and mediatore-claim-<uid>, labelled app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=mediatore. Shape enforced at admission by CEL policy: spiffeID under /banlieue/, parentID a tpm agent with the same EK hash, unix selectors only, no admin/downstream/storeSVID. Auditable through the API server audit log and restorable from a cluster backup (ADR-0006).

nodes.name: SPIRE Agent + SPIFFE CSI driver (k8s node)
nodes.description: Per-node DaemonSets from the hardened chart. The agent attests the node with k8s_psat, attests pods through a kubelet whose serving certificate it verifies, and serves the Workload API on a hostPath socket directory. The CSI driver bind-mounts that directory read-only into pods that declare a csi.spiffe.io inline volume, so no workload needs a hostPath. Both are node-level TCB, the same tier as the kubelet (ADR-0007).

nodes.name: SPIRE Root Server (desired state)
nodes.description: Root of the trust domain on the dedicated identity cluster: HA, PostgreSQL-backed, CA keyed through an UpstreamAuthority plugin against an HSM / KMS / corporate PKI. Issues intermediate CAs to downstream servers only; no agent or workload talks to it directly. Elided in the homelab collapse (ADR-0005).

nodes.name: Identity Cluster (desired state)
nodes.description: Dedicated cluster (auth.example.com style) owned by the identity/security team, with its own change control. Hosts only the SPIRE root and its datastore; sandbox-cluster administrators have no access here (ADR-0005).

nodes.name: Management Cluster
nodes.description: The banlieue management cluster: runs mediatore, the downstream SPIRE server with its controller manager, the SPIRE agent and SPIFFE CSI driver DaemonSets, the Kubernetes API and the banlieue controllers. In the homelab this is the single banlieue cluster and the downstream server is the only SPIRE server.

nodes.name: Sandbox VM (pool member)
nodes.description: A banlieue pool member with a fresh vTPM, attested at boot before any claim exists. Carries the SPIRE agent, the in-guest agent and, once bound, the jailed workload.

nodes.name: SPIRE Agent (in guest)
nodes.description: Attests the node with the vTPM EK certificate and serves the Workload API socket, the only credential surface inside the jail.

nodes.name: mediatore guest
nodes.description: Root daemon, the guest role of the one mediatore binary (ADR-0014): registers the node (EK hash + DMI UUID), polls GET /v1/me for a bound claim, creates the per-subject user (sb- + 12 hex, ADR-0004), builds /mnt/sandbox, bind-mounts the binary at the pinned path read-only into the jail and supervises the nsjail until the deadline, then tears down. crates/mediatore-guest.

nodes.name: Jailed Workload
nodes.description: Runs under nsjail as the per-subject user with only the Workload API socket mounted in. Fetches its claim SVID and trades it at POST /v1/token for one short-lived, audience-scoped token at a time (mediatore token, the same binary mounted read-only into the jail; ADR-0014). No token ever rests on disk.

nodes.name: Downstream APIs
nodes.description: Services the sandbox may call on the user's behalf: Entra-protected APIs (OBO tokens) or JWKS-validating services (STS tokens with the act claim). Each validates audience and can audit 'broker on behalf of user'.

nodes.name: Sandbox Network Segment
nodes.description: Pool members' network. Egress only: SPIRE server (TCP 8081), mediatore's sandbox listener (TCP 443) and the allowed downstream APIs. Nothing inbound to the VM; Kube API and SPIRE server are unreachable from inside the jail.

relationships.description: The mediatore system is one binary composed of the two API surfaces, the claim watcher and the STS; the claim store and the STS signing key are the state it guards.
Everything identity-bearing on a pool member: the SPIRE agent (node identity), the in-guest agent (subject plumbing) and the jailed workload (claim identity).
Pool members live on the egress-only sandbox segment.

Everything control-plane-side shares the management cluster; the SPIRE downstream server, its controller manager and the per-node agent and CSI driver are scoped to it so entry rendering, k8s_psat validation and pod attestation stay per-environment.
The root SPIRE server lives alone on the identity cluster; the root signing key never resides where sandboxes are administered.

Nested SPIRE: the downstream server obtains its intermediate CA from the root and chains every SVID it issues to the one trust domain. Revoking the intermediate cuts an entire environment off from above. Absent in the homelab collapse (ADR-0005).
The user logs in at the IdP (PKCE via mediatore login or az login) and receives a token whose audience is mediatore. The user's token is only ever presented to mediatore, never to the VM.

POST /v1/claims with the IdP bearer token creates an AgentSandbox with the token's subject (ADR-0008); GET answers from its status, DELETE deletes it. Subject equality is enforced on read and delete. For a session issuer the request also carries the caller's refresh token (mediatore login, PKCE as client mediatore; ADR-0013), which is sealed with the AgentSandbox UID into a sessions row before the response and follows the claim into its record; it never touches the resource.

JWKS discovery and signature validation for incoming tokens; for a session issuer (ADR-0013, built), a refresh_token grant before every token issue, as mediatore's own public client: the fresh ID token is validated like a login (group gate included), the rotated refresh token re-sealed into the record, and invalid_grant releases the claim at once. For an Entra issuer (ADR-0016, built): the On-Behalf-Of exchange of the caller's access token at claim creation (offline_access, the first entra-obo audience or mediatore's own resource), mediatore authenticating with a PS256 client assertion signed by a key file, by OpenBao transit, or presented as a projected ServiceAccount token under workload identity federation; before every issue a refresh_token grant naming the audience's resource, a token for mediatore itself validated like a login for an sts audience, Entra's token handed to the workload as is for an entra-obo audience. The user's original token is discarded after validation.

Creates the AgentSandbox with spec.subject from the validated token (ADR-0008); the reconciler, not the user API, creates the VirtualMachineClaim. The mediatore ServiceAccount is exempt from the caller-equals-subject check of the agentsandbox-subject policy because it acts for subjects it has validated tokens for, and is listed as a broker in banlieue's claim-subject policy.

Watches VirtualMachineClaim (label app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=mediatore) for Bound / Releasing / Failed / deletion and VirtualMachine (banlieue.io/pool) for a published vTPM endorsement certificate; binds by the EK hash the claim mirrors, fails an unresolved bind after 60 s by deleting the claim, declares node entries from members (ADR-0011). Runs on the replica holding the coordination.k8s.io Lease mediatore-watcher.

Watches AgentSandbox and creates, owns and deletes its one VirtualMachineClaim through the Kubernetes API with the broker ServiceAccount (ADR-0008, built). RBAC: get/list/watch/patch/create/delete on agentsandboxes, patch on agentsandboxes/status and update on agentsandboxes/finalizers; create/delete/get/list/watch on virtualmachineclaims. Never patches a pool member: binding stays in banlieue's claim controller.
An AgentSandbox is the sandbox user's request, attributed to them by admission; the claim, entry and tokens all derive from it.
banlieue's claim controller binds Ready pool members to claims and destroys members on release; mediatore only observes the results. CRDs are the entire interface.

Declares the claim entry (parent = the bound VM's tpm agent ID, selector unix:user:sb-<hash>) as a ClusterStaticEntry on Bound and deletes it on release, through the Kubernetes API with the broker ServiceAccount. RBAC: create/delete/get/list/watch on clusterstaticentries only; the mediatore-clusterstaticentry admission policy rejects any other shape. Waits for status.set. No gRPC, no admin SVID (ADR-0006).
Watches ClusterSPIFFEID and ClusterStaticEntry resources and reports rendering status on them.

Unix domain socket, not a network protocol (CALM's protocol enum has no value for it). Renders declared resources into registration entries over the server's private Unix socket inside the pod. The admin API is never exposed on the network.

Unix domain socket, not a network protocol (CALM's protocol enum has no value for it). The broker pod fetches spiffe://<td>/mediatore and the trust-domain bundle from the node's SPIRE agent over the Workload API socket, mounted read-only by the SPIFFE CSI driver (no hostPath). SVID and key stay in process memory and rotate on the stream (ADR-0007).
k8s_psat node attestation with a projected, audience-bound ServiceAccount token, then SVID fetching for attested pods.
TPM node attestation at boot (EK certificate + credential activation), then SVID rotation. Claim-independent: a warm member is attested before any claim exists.
POST /v1/nodes (EK hash + DMI UUID + hostname) over the node SVID at boot; then polls GET /v1/me until a claim is bound and the subject comes back.

POST /v1/token over the claim SVID: one audience per request, from the claim's allowlist, capped at 15 minutes, never a refresh token. Rate-limited per claim (token.rate_per_minute, 429 beyond it) ahead of any upstream call (ADR-0013).
The sandbox calls a downstream API with the audience-scoped token; the API's audit log records both the user and the broker (azp / act).
The subject a claim is issued for; the user only ever sees their own claims. The row outlives nothing: a claim that ended is swept into the audit table after store.retention_secs (ADR-0012).

Every store read and write from both API surfaces and the reconcilers: the record on create, the entry id and deadline on bind, revocation on release, the node registry on registration, the sweep into the audit table at resync (ADR-0012). TLS verify-full to PostgreSQL; a file for SQLite.

Seal and unseal of refresh material (ADR-0015): encrypt when a session is parked at claim creation, decrypt and encrypt again on every token issue (the refresh of ADR-0013), under a derived transit key with the sandbox UID as context. The broker logs in with its projected ServiceAccount token (audience openbao) and keeps the OpenBao token in memory until its lease ends. TLS 1.3 verified against store.sealing.transit.ca_file; a probe seal at startup fails the process on a wrong role, policy or key. With issuers[].entra.transit (ADR-0016) the broker also asks transit to sign its client assertion for Entra (PSS, SHA-256) with an RSA key that never leaves OpenBao.
Declared registration entries are state the watcher owns and the controller manager consumes; a sweep deletes any whose claim is gone.

flows.name: Claim a sandbox and act as the user
flows.description: The happy path from login to a delegated downstream call: login, claim, bind, subject fetch, jail, token.

transitions.description: User logs in; receives a token with aud = mediatore.
POST /v1/claims; mediatore validates the token and derives the subject.
mediatore creates an AgentSandbox with spec.subject; its reconciler creates the owned VirtualMachineClaim and the store record keyed by the claim's UID (ADR-0008).
banlieue binds a Ready, already-attested pool member and mirrors its EK certificate onto the claim.
The watcher hashes the EK certificate's public key, resolves the node, and declares the claim's ClusterStaticEntry (admission policy checks the shape).
The controller manager renders the entry over the private socket and reports status.set; the watcher marks the claim live.
The in-guest agent fetches the subject over its node SVID, creates the sb- user and starts the jail.
The workload presents its claim SVID over mTLS and trades it for a short-lived, audience-scoped token.
The workload calls the downstream API on the user's behalf.

flows.name: Release and cut-off
flows.description: Any of four independent cut-offs stops the sandbox acting as the user; this is the ordered normal release.

transitions.description: DELETE /v1/claims (or the TTL fires). The store row is revoked: /v1/token refuses immediately.
The ClusterStaticEntry is deleted; the controller manager removes the server entry and the workload's SVID stops within the agent sync interval.
The VirtualMachineClaim is deleted (or its deletion observed).
banlieue destroys the member, vTPM included; the guest agent tears down the jail and user regardless.

flows.name: Node bootstrap: from EK certificate to node SVID
flows.description: How a fresh pool member gets the in-guest agent's identity without the broker ever listing agents or holding a SPIRE admin credential (ADR-0006, ADR-0007).

transitions.description: banlieue publishes the member's vTPM EK certificate on VirtualMachine.status (banlieue ADR-0045) before GuestReady.
The watcher computes sha256(DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo) of the EK, which is the tpm attestor's agent ID hash, and declares mediatore-node-<ek-hash> parented to that agent.
The controller manager renders the node entry; it waits in the server until the agent attests.
The VM's agent attests with the EK; on sync it receives the node entry and issues the node SVID to the guest role (unix:uid:0 and the path of the one mediatore binary).
mediatore guest registers the node over mTLS with that SVID; the broker checks the SVID's EK hash equals the registered one and refuses a cloned EK with 409.

metadata.project: mediatore — identity broker for banlieue sandbox VMs
metadata.phase: dev-mode loop implemented and e2e-tested; Entra OBO is a fail-closed stub. Roadmap 01 (ADR-0006, ADR-0007) implemented and live-tested in kind: registration entries as ClusterStaticEntry through the Kubernetes API, broker identity from the Workload API over the SPIFFE CSI driver, SPIFFE mTLS terminated in-process (crates/mediatore-tls). Roadmap 03 (ADR-0011): the claim watcher, node resolution by EK, node entries from pool members, leader election by Lease. Roadmap 08 (ADR-0008): the AgentSandbox CRD, its reconciler on the same loop, the subject admission policy and the user API creating the resource; records now exist outside dev_mode. SPIRE topology models the ADR-0005 desired state: root on a dedicated identity cluster, downstream per environment; the homelab collapses to the downstream server alone. Roadmap 05 (ADR-0012): one sqlx store over SQLite or PostgreSQL, the sealed refresh envelope, rows swept into an audit table; every kind tier runs the broker on PostgreSQL over verify-full. Roadmap 04, first slice (ADR-0013): the Dex path, with the upstream session delegated at claim creation, sealed, refreshed before every issue and revoked on refusal; mediatore-cli; per-claim rate limiting. Entra OBO and the transit sealer are the roadmap's next slices. ADR-0014: one binary, the roles as subcommands (serve, guest, token, login, sandbox, session), one musl artifact for every host, the jail mounting it read-only; the node entry pins /usr/local/bin/mediatore. ADR-0015: the transit sealer; the kind tiers run the broker on an OpenBao (make kind-openbao) with Kubernetes auth and a derived key; the local sealer stays the homelab shape. ADR-0016: the Entra path, with the caller's token exchanged On-Behalf-Of at claim creation, the session refreshed per audience before every issue, and the broker's credential a signed assertion (key file, OpenBao transit or a federated ServiceAccount token); proven against the fake issuer, the live run against a tenant is by hand. ADR-0017: issuer profiles, the session path for any OIDC issuer (Google and Auth0 beside Dex), per-issuer login parameters and groups claim. ADR-0018: TPM attestation with the SPIFFE community plugin as a kustomize component, the hypervisors' swtpm CAs as the EK bundle; the agent fragments for the VM image.
